replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: Start with an equation like ax² + bx + c = 0. Factor out 'a' first: x² + (b/a)x + (c/a) = 0. Use the quadratic formula—x = [-b ± √(b² – 4ac)] / 2a—to isolate solutions. Verify by plugging back into original terms; errors often highlight where my neuroticism might overcomplicate verification!

Stationary points occur where dy/dx = 0. First differentiate f(x) to get f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x-coordinates. For concavity checks, plug these x-values into the second derivative (f’’(x)). Double-check by plotting—my anxiety sometimes leads me to overlook sign changes!
